title: Dance halls and winning the slow drag contest
summary: He lists the halls where he danced, explains how he got the name Slow Drag, and tells of a chalk-mark dance bet won with a hurt foot for a fifteen dollar prize.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You tell good stories, man. Yes, I do.
But don't forget now, I used to dance. I was going to ask you about the dancing and where you used to dance. Where were these?

Yeah, I mean, I used to dance. I mean, at Economy Hall, Hope's Hall, Globes Hall, Masonic Hall, New Hall, Funzami Hall. I didn't bother nobody. Didn't bother from a zooka pool, no. But I used to dance more, I used to dance more, I'd get my kicks out of it, and slow drag dance. And about me dance slow drag dance, and they kept on saying, I love slow drag, the dance. Well, they kept that name called me slow drag, you see, and that's when they kept that name. Yeah, I used to have a nice time. Well, let the Lord bless you, and I'm glad you all come see me.
I was going to ask a little bit more, if you have time, about the slow drag. Did you dance that with just one girl, or did you go around in a circle?

One girl, one girl, see, everybody got to have a couple, I mean a couple, see. Just like you would have a lady, you would have a lady with your dancing. And the one with the dance that slow drag the bass, we won the prize. You know, that's when my prize got soon. He used to be a good dancer too. We had a ball called 88, he wanted to throw around and show me that he beat me dancing. I was working painting, I stuck a piece of pine wood in my foot, it must have been about two weeks. A piece of what? Pound wood, I mean, yeah, coming out the leather, you know what I mean, you're sticking out. Litter. And my brother over there and got soon one to us, we're going to catch this. He said, uh-uh, uh-uh, ain't got nothing to do with this. I'm going to win this bet and give me the money or you got to shove it down. So I went and told him, my mother took a piece of rag and took a needle. I told him about me poor, the whole wood come out, but a piece broke in there. About five days or six days after, she'd never even talk. And my mother told me, I said, my mother couldn't walk on that. My mother turned on that and pet me, my sister pet me, and she don't let me even let that stuff come out and she squeezed it. And I passed away for a while, I mean, got weak, you know. Two to about a day and a half after, I turned on that. The more I walk on, I feel better, you know. When I kept on walking, I felt good, you know. So my brother, I said, look, let that go of him. I said, I got him. I said, I got as soon as to let it go. I said, one thing I want you to do. I said, what? I just want me and my lady is going to be here. I want you to take a chalk and mark it right down there. Well, him and his lady right there, I'm going to just take a chalk and mark it down. When the band start, he's going to be in front, I'll be in front. But when the band start, when the band stop, I'm going to start just where that chalk is. Now, if you stop, that would be a door, but you see. Now, if you stop, if I stop, I mean, pass my mark, chalk, and you stop there, and make me, and the first thing in the band, I saw a fool, and I know the time. I know when the band going to stop, and I know a fool. Then I turn around there, and I see where I go, and I slide down, and I turn it around the bench, and I turn it around the bench, and I like doing a chalk, right, chalk? You think chalk like this, where over there? I see. Cheap pop, what you think the bed was? How much? Fifteen dollars. Oh, I know. And the man went nothing, but the bed was on the outside. The lady, the lady get the umbrella. Every team thought I'd win the best, I mean, you don't get nothing.
The umbrella was the prize. Yeah, the lady gets that, you don't get that.
